meta.title: Yojana Sathi — Scheme Eligibility Dataset (v1)
meta.purpose: Source-of-truth dataset for the eligibility-matching engine built for MPOnline Idea & Innovation Hackathon 2026, Challenge 5 (AI Innovation for Public Services & Citizen-Centric Governance).
meta.compiled_from: Public scheme-explainer sources (buddy4study, myscheme.gov.in, vikaspedia, official portals referenced within). NOT scraped from official government APIs.
meta.disclaimer: This is a proof-of-concept dataset for a hackathon prototype, not a legal or authoritative source. Income limits, percentage cutoffs and stipend amounts on real government schemes change frequently and sometimes vary slightly across secondary sources. Every 'official_portal' URL below must be treated as the actual source of truth — the app's UI must visibly say 'verify on the official portal before applying' next to every result. Do not add schemes to this file without a citation; do not let the LLM invent new schemes at runtime.

schemes.name_en: Post-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST/OBC Students (MP Scholarship Portal 2.0 / MPTAAS)
schemes.department: Tribal Welfare Dept. / Social Justice Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Monthly financial assistance for SC, ST and OBC students enrolled in post-matric (Class 11 onward, including UG/PG/diploma/professional courses) at a recognised institution in MP.

other_conditions: Enrolled in a recognised institution in India
Some sub-schemes cite an income ceiling closer to ₹6,00,000 for specific categories — verify current ceiling for your exact category on the portal

schemes.benefits: Approx. ₹500/month for 10 months (varies by sub-scheme and course level); ST students apply specifically via the MPTAAS portal.
schemes.notes: Two overlapping portals exist historically (scholarshipportal.mp.nic.in legacy and hescholarship.mp.gov.in current) — confirm the live one before demo.

schemes.department: Higher Education Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Small annual scholarship for meritorious General-category students from low-income families pursuing higher education.

other_conditions: At least 60% marks in Class 12
Sources differ on exact income tiers (₹54,000 vs ₹1,20,000 for some course levels) — treat ₹54,000 as the conservative default and flag the higher tier as 'possibly eligible, verify'

schemes.notes: Low benefit amount — good for demoing 'small but real' schemes many citizens don't know exist.

schemes.department: Higher Education Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Scholarship for meritorious girls from rural Madhya Pradesh to support their higher education.

other_conditions: At least 60% marks in Class 12
Must reside in a rural area of MP

schemes.department: Tribal/Social Justice Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Hostel/residence financial support for SC/ST students who must live away from home to study.

other_conditions: Enrolled in a higher education institution away from permanent residence, with no hostel seat available

schemes.benefits: Fixed annual allowance toward accommodation costs (amount varies; verify on portal).
required_documents: Proof that no hostel seat was allotted
schemes.notes: Good example scheme for the 'lesser-known' narrative in your pitch.

schemes.department: Higher Education Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Flagship merit scholarship covering tuition fees (govt. college) or a large fixed amount (private college) for high-scoring Class 12 students entering undergraduate courses.

other_conditions: MP Board Class 12: ~70-75% marks (sources vary — verify current cutoff); CBSE/ICSE: ~85%
Engineering aspirants: JEE Main rank below 1,50,000 (some sources say 50,000 — verify)
Medical aspirants: admission via NEET to a govt./private medical/dental/AYUSH college
Law aspirants: qualified CLAT, admission to an NLU

schemes.benefits: Full tuition fee reimbursement (government colleges) or up to ₹1.5 lakh/year (private colleges).
schemes.notes: High-value, high-visibility scheme — strong demo candidate for a 'high school topper' persona.

schemes.name_en: Mukhya Mantri Jan Kalyan (Sambal) Yojana — Scholarship for Unorganised Workers' Children
schemes.summary: Scholarship for wards of unorganised-sector workers registered under the Sambal Yojana, covering UG/diploma/polytechnic/ITI, with special provisions for engineering, medical and law aspirants.

other_conditions: Parent/guardian must be registered as an unorganised worker under the Sambal/Labour Dept. scheme
Engineering aspirants: JEE Main rank below 1,50,000
Medical aspirants: admission via JIPMER/AIIMS/NEET
Law aspirants: admission via CLAT

schemes.benefits: Course fee support, similar structure to MMVY, scaled to unorganised-worker households.
schemes.notes: Requires parent's Sambal registration as a precondition — a good example of a scheme with a 'hidden prerequisite' that citizens often miss, worth calling out explicitly in the UI.

schemes.department: Women & Child Development Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Staged financial-assistance scheme for girl children born in MP, paying out at school milestones (Class 6/9/11/12) and a lump sum at age 21, aimed at preventing school drop-out and child marriage.

eligibility.residency: Parents are domicile of Madhya Pradesh
other_conditions: Girl child born on or after 1 January 2006
Registration must be done within one year of birth — NOT retroactively available for older girls who were never registered
Parents must not be income-tax payers
Family-planning condition applies from the second child onward

schemes.benefits: ₹6,000/year for first 5 years (₹30,000 total), ₹2,000 at Class 6, ₹4,000 at Class 9, ₹7,500 at Class 11, ₹200/month during Class 11-12, and a lump sum around ₹1 lakh at age 21 (subject to not being married before 18); Ladli Laxmi 2.0 adds ~₹25,000 for graduation/professional courses.
schemes.notes: IMPORTANT eligibility trap for your matching logic: a girl over ~1 year old who was never registered as an infant is NOT eligible now, even if she meets every other criterion. Model this as a hard disqualifier, not just an age check.

schemes.department: Women & Child Development Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Unconditional monthly cash transfer to economically weaker married/widowed/divorced/abandoned women in MP.

other_conditions: Not an income-tax payer (or family member of one)
No family member in regular government employment
Family does not own more than 5 acres of agricultural land
Family does not own a four-wheeler
Not already receiving ₹1,000+/month under another government pension scheme (partial top-up possible if receiving less)

schemes.notes: One of MP's largest-scale schemes (1.29+ crore beneficiaries) — good for a 'why does the citizen not already know about this' framing in your pitch.

schemes.department: Women & Child Development Dept. / Housing, Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: Housing assistance for existing Ladli Behna beneficiaries who are homeless or living in a kutcha/damaged house and are not covered by PMAY.

other_conditions: Must already be an active Ladli Behna Yojana beneficiary
Must be homeless or living in a kutcha/damaged house
Must be excluded from the PMAY beneficiary list

schemes.benefits: ₹2,00,000 for constructing a pucca house, released in 3 installments.
schemes.notes: Good example of a 'dependent scheme' — your matching engine should only surface this if the user already qualifies for Ladli Behna, and should say so explicitly.

schemes.name_en: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students
schemes.department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (via National Scholarship Portal)
schemes.summary: Central Sector Scheme covering full tuition and approved course fees for ST students in graduate/postgraduate courses at Ministry-notified premier institutions.

other_conditions: Admission to one of ~265 Ministry-notified premier institutions
Income rule: orphans exempt from income limit; married candidates' spouse income included; siblings' income excluded

schemes.benefits: Full tuition + approved course fees, continued for the course duration subject to satisfactory performance.

schemes.name_en: Central Sector / UGC Scholarship Schemes (via National Scholarship Portal)
schemes.department: Ministry of Electronics & IT / respective line ministries (via NSP)
schemes.summary: Umbrella category for the 100+ central, state and UGC scholarship schemes hosted on the National Scholarship Portal, spanning Class 1 through PhD.

other_conditions: At least 50% marks in the previous qualifying exam
Requires One-Time Registration (OTR) on NSP, Aadhaar-linked bank account

schemes.benefits: Varies widely by specific scheme: ₹1,000-5,000/year (pre-matric) up to ₹80,000/year (post-matric/UGC/professional).
schemes.notes: Treat this as a 'catch-all' bucket in the demo — flag it whenever a user doesn't cleanly fit a named MP state scheme but is a student under the income ceiling, and be explicit in the UI that the exact sub-scheme still needs to be selected on NSP itself.

schemes.department: Technical Education & Skill Development Dept., Govt. of MP
schemes.summary: On-the-job training scheme for educated-but-unemployed youth in registered industrial/commercial establishments, with a monthly stipend during training and a recognised certificate afterward.

other_conditions: Must have completed formal education (12th/ITI/diploma/graduate) — currently enrolled full-time students are not eligible
Must be currently unemployed / not in a job

schemes.benefits: Monthly stipend: ₹8,000 (12th pass), ₹8,500 (ITI), ₹9,000 (diploma), ₹10,000 (graduate+), largely via DBT; SCVT certificate on completion.
schemes.notes: This is the one scheme in the dataset outside pure 'education/scholarship' — use it to demonstrate the tool also covers the Recruitment/Employability domain named in the challenge brief.

schemes.name_en: Ayushman Bharat — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
schemes.department: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
schemes.summary: Cashless hospitalisation cover of ₹5 lakh/family/year for secondary and tertiary care at empanelled hospitals, for economically vulnerable families identified via SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, plus a universal cover for all seniors 70+.

other_conditions: Family identified under SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, OR holds a valid BPL/Antyodaya ration card, OR
Any individual aged 70+ is eligible regardless of income (via a separate Ayushman Vay Vandana Card)

schemes.benefits: ₹5,00,000 per family per year, cashless, family-floater basis; additional ₹5,00,000 top-up exclusively for 70+ members already covered under a family card.
required_documents: Ration card (BPL/Antyodaya) or SECC entitlement letter
schemes.application_mode: online (via Ayushman App/portal) or at empanelled hospital
schemes.notes: The only genuinely nationwide, non-education scheme in this v1 dataset — useful to show the model generalises beyond scholarships if you extend scope in a later phase.

test_personas.name: Aarti — rural OBC undergraduate
test_personas.why: OBC + rural + under relevant income ceilings covers post-matric and NSP; 65% doesn't clear MMVY's ~70-75% cutoff; Vikramaditya is General-category only; too young for Ladli Behna.

test_personas.name: Ramesh — unemployed ITI graduate
test_personas.why: Fits Seekho Kamao's age/education/unemployment criteria exactly; not a current student so post-matric scholarships don't apply; male, so Ladli Behna doesn't apply.

test_personas.name: Sunita — married woman, low income
test_personas.why: Meets every Ladli Behna condition; Awas Yojana additionally requires already being a beneficiary AND homeless/kutcha housing, which isn't stated here — matcher should ask a follow-up question rather than assume.

test_personas.name: Neha — infant girl, just born
test_personas.why: Textbook Ladli Laxmi case — use this persona to test the registration-timing disqualifier logic against an older, unregistered-girl counter-example.
